claims.text: The application must run the underwriting pipeline as an explicit multi-stage workflow: intake → document extraction → financial spreading → risk grading → memo drafting → policy compliance check → tiered approval → closing.
Each pipeline stage's status must be visible on a pipeline board.
An intake triage agent must classify incoming requests.
The intake triage agent must flag missing documents.
The intake triage agent must route incoming requests to the right analyst queue.
A financial spreading agent must extract figures from borrower financial statements into the standard spread template.
The financial spreading agent must show its source for every extracted number.
A credit memo agent must draft the underwriting memo, citing the specific ratios, spread figures, and policy rules it relied on.
A policy compliance agent must review every drafted memo against lending policy, including concentration limits, prohibited industries, and loan-to-value caps.
The policy compliance agent must raise written exceptions when policy violations are found.
A portfolio Q&A agent must let credit officers ask questions across active deals (e.g. "show me all deals above $500k with DSCR under 1.2").
The portfolio Q&A agent's answers must be grounded in stored deal data.
Deterministic logic — never an agent — must compute the credit ratios: DSCR, leverage, and current ratio.
Deterministic logic — never an agent — must assign the risk grade from a transparent rubric.
Approvals must be tiered by exposure: a credit analyst may approve up to $250k.
Approvals must be tiered by exposure: a senior credit officer may approve up to $1M.
Approvals must be tiered by exposure: a credit committee must approve deals above $1M.
No agent may ever approve, decline, or advance a deal past an approval step.
A named human decision is mandatory at each approval step.
Every agent output (triage, spread, memo, compliance exceptions) requires human acceptance before the workflow proceeds.
Declined deals require a documented adverse-action reason.
Every state change, ratio calculation, agent draft, and human decision must land in an immutable audit trail.
Role-based access must separate relationship managers, who may submit deals and view only their own deals.
Role-based access must separate credit analysts, who may spread financials, draft memos, and recommend decisions.
Role-based access must separate credit officers, who may approve, decline, or return deals for rework.
Deals idle past 5 business days must surface on an SLA dashboard.
Applications currently arrive as emails and spreadsheets, so intake/document extraction must accommodate those formats.
The system must be deployed to a local target.
Supervision mode is gates-only, meaning human approval gates are required at defined checkpoints rather than continuous supervision.
No supporting documents were supplied beyond the problem statement (documents_dir is none); all requirements derive from the intake problem statement itself.
